title: Barcelona Injuries: Every Player Unavailable vs. Real Madrid
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath2:00 PM EDTJules Koundé is a major doubt for the weekend. / Fran Santiago/Getty ImagesIt could be a season-defining Clásico when Barcelona meet Real Madrid on Sunday.
Hansi Flick’s men have been faultless in La Liga after nine games and have the chance to go nine points clear of their great rivals with a win at Camp Nou this weekend.
While victory far from ends the title race, it would strike a deep psychological blow to Madrid and make Barcelona the first team in history to open the season with 10 straight wins.

Barça would naturally want to count on all their key players for such a pivotal game. However, Flick has several availability concerns to deal with. Here are all the injury issues the team is contending with ahead of the clash.

Roony Bardghji was struck down in preseason. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesIssue: ACL injuryPotential return date: May 2027The young Swedish winger suffered an anterior cruciate ligament tear in preseason training is set to spend the entire campaign in recovery.
Bardghji was rumored to have been deemed surplus to requirements by Flick and could well be moved on when he returns to full fitness.

Andreas Christensen could return next month. / Fran Santiago/Getty ImagesIssue: Thigh injuryPotential return date: November 2026After missing more than half of last season with a serious knee injury, Christensen picked up a thigh strain in September and is set to be sidelined for over a month.
The center back, who has made six appearances so far in 2026–27, is slated to return to action after the November international break.

Eric García’s knock comes at an unfortunate time. / Gabriel Colchero/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesIssue: Thigh injuryPotential return date: November 2026García left the field in discomfort during the 5–2 win away at Real Betis and was later confirmed to have picked up a thigh issue.

The club put his recovery timeline at between three and four weeks, ruling him out of the clash with Real Madrid and likely to return either just before the November international break, or straight after.

Dani Olmo was forced off against PSG. / Ibrahim Ezzat/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesIssue: Adductor injuryPotential return date: November 2026Olmo was a casualty of Barcelona’s 4–2 Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain midweek, limping off in the first half and sparking fears over his availability for the weekend’s showdown with Madrid.
Barça later confirmed an adductor injury and have suggested the midfielder will be out for around a month as he recovers.

Two Barça right backs picked up injuries against Betis. / Gabriel Colchero/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesIssue: Ankle injuryPotential return date: October 2026Koundé was one of two right-back injuries during the Betis victory, along with García, creating a potential headache for Flick in the build up to the Clásico.

“We hope that maybe he [Koundé] could also be an option for the weekend, but we have to see. We have to wait,” Flick told reporters regarding the Frenchman’s minor ankle sprain, but that was before he missed even more training sessions.
